analysis: The broad economics option combines microeconomics, macroeconomics, public economics and econometrics with business, accounting, consumer engagement and organisational behaviour. Programming, linear algebra, probability and applied data methods strengthen its quantitative core. Qualitative research complements market and organisational inquiry through interviewing and document analysis.

The public economics option connects public goods, welfare and redistribution to comparative institutions, law and policy implementation. Legal foundations precede constitutional and EU law. Sustainability governance and persuasion introduce policy instruments, collective action and public communication. Sociology and ethics support the study of inequality and responsibility, with economics and empirical methods retained.

The finance option combines accounting, interest rates, banking, financial markets and open-economy macroeconomics. International business law contributes trade finance and cross-border contracts. Probability, numerical methods, econometrics and programming provide methods for analysing financial data. General AI decision models add methods for uncertainty without suggesting dedicated financial machine learning.

Pairwise differences are 82.5, 37.5 and 105 EC each way. Changes resolve six offering conflicts and one earlier legal prerequisite conflict. The finance option remains distinct from the broad option through dedicated numerical and computational work and the legal and institutional context of cross-border financial decisions. The public option has a distinct focus on economic policy and institutions. Separate UvA research, theory and thesis components are retained without treating partial overlaps as equivalences.
constructionStop: Three coherent, distinct options reach the programme limit.
